description: Plants, fells and hauls timber from a woodlot outside the walls
materialRequirements: A Forester's Post outside the walls, and room for trees to fall

productions.description: Fells trees at the woodlot and hauls the wood home

interdependenceDescription: Timber feeds the Carpenter's work; the Blacksmith keeps the axes sharp
randomTalk: Every tree is just a very slow log that hasn't been told yet.
The trick to felling is deciding where it lands BEFORE you start. The trick to my technique is remembering that.
People ask if I talk to the trees. I do. It's a short conversation and I do most of it with an axe.
There's a birch out past the wall that's been leaning the wrong way for six years. We have an understanding. Neither of us moves first.
Sap gets everywhere. In the beard, in the stew, in places I will not be discussing.
A sharp axe does the work. A dull axe does nothing.
I planted a sapling last spring. It's doing nothing. Magnificent, uninterrupted nothing. I'm very proud.
The Carpenter wants straight timber. The forest grows what it likes. We've agreed to be disappointed in each other.
You can tell a lot about a person by how they stack wood. I'm not saying what. I'm just saying I've noticed.
Never stand downhill of a log. That's not wisdom, that's just geometry.
The greydwarves take it personally when I fell a tree. I've stopped apologising. It wasn't helping.
Fir splits clean. Pine splits mean. Oak splits when it feels it's earned the right.
I count rings sometimes. Some of these trees were here before the village. Before me. They don't seem smug about it, which I appreciate.
My back has opinions about this profession. My back is not in charge.
Two things fall in this forest: trees, and people who weren't watching the trees.
Resin is bitter, difficult to get off, and slightly fermented.  A lot like myself actually.
I don't chop firewood angry. I chop it thoroughly. There's a difference and the wood knows it.
The stumps remember. Walk the woodlot and you can read the whole season in them.
randomGreets: Mind the drop line, friend. Trees don't check who's standing there.
Well met! Don't lean on that stack, it's not as settled as it looks.
Ah, a visitor. Stand upwind, I've been at the resin.
Hello! If you hear cracking, walk toward me, not away. Trust me on this.
Greetings. Mind your feet — half this ground is root and the other half is opinion.
Come to watch? Grand. Just stay behind the post and we'll both go home whole.
randomGoodbye: Off with you. I've a birch that's been asking for it all morning.
Safe travels! Keep an eye up when you're under branches.
Right, back to it. The forest isn't going to fall over on its own. Mostly.
Farewell. If you pass the woodlot, don't touch the leaning one.
Go on then. I'll be here, making tall things shorter.
